sources.entry: Interview: Sweep founders share learnings from building an AI coding assistant

summary.name: Sweep
summary.one_liner: Sweep is an open-source AI coding agent (YC S23) that turns GitHub issues into pull requests, as described in an E2B interview with its founders.
use_cases: turning GitHub bug reports into pull requests
generating feature code from issue tickets
iterating on AI-generated pull requests via comments
studying challenges of building coding agents
summary.what_it_does: Sweep watches GitHub issues and, when labeled "sweep", plans a solution, writes code, and opens it as a pull request without an IDE. It uses embedding-based code search to find relevant code in the repository. Users can comment on the pull request to iterate on the result. The page says initial startup takes about 3-5 minutes depending on codebase size, and usage is around 100 pull requests a day. The founders describe most agent failures as coming from non-prompt issues, and they debug by visualizing agent conversation logs with an internal chat visualizer.
notable: Open source, with over 5000 GitHub stars per the page
Turns GitHub issues directly into pull requests without an IDE
Triggered by adding the 'sweep' label to an issue
Team limits GPT-4 usage to 5 uses a month, with the rest on GPT-3.5
caveats: Users cannot view the internal debugging visualization and must contact the Sweep team, about once a day
Architecture is server-centralized; if servers have an issue, all users are affected
Usage is limited by design to encourage work-related use
